title: Drupal reports core flaw CVE-2026-132165 exploited on live sites; fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13
summary: Drupal rates SA-CORE-2026-017, CVE-2026-132165, highly critical: under specific conditions install.php can be used to reinstall a site, leading to takeover or code execution. Drupal's advisory update says it received a report of exploitation on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. CISA added CVE-2026-132165 to its known-exploited catalog on 24 November. NSFOCUS (27 November) says a proof of concept is publicly available.
plain: Drupal fixed a serious flaw that can let an attacker take over a website by re-running its installer, and says it has a report of the flaw being exploited on live sites.
exec: Drupal has a report that this highly critical flaw was exploited on live sites; Drupal sites on older versions need its fix.
action: Drupal advises updating core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13; if you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes. Older branches are end of life, per Drupal.

key_findings: SA-CORE-2026-017 (Highly critical, CVE-2026-132165): installer reinstall leading to takeover or RCE; advisory update reports exploitation on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC.
SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166) is a gadget chain needing a separate unsafe-unserialize flaw.
recommendations: Upgrade; secure the installer if you cannot.

validation.note: Read Drupal SA-CORE-2026-017 and SA-CORE-2026-018 (Drupal Security Team, primary) and the CISA alert of 24 November (CISA, authority); Drupal and CISA each state CVE-2026-132165. Advisory 017 re-read on 25 November: carries the exploitation update.
